subject: Finex integration: API creds ops handoff & rotation schedule
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.inference>
To: Ritika Sharma <ritika@finex.io>
Cc: Samir Desai <samir@finex.io>
Date: 2027-08-22T15:06:00-07:00
Subject: Finex integration: post-demo handoff — auth + routing options

Hi Ritika / Samir,

Thanks again for your time today — appreciate the clear view into Finex's workflows (real-time routing for risk alerts + nightly batch enrichment). Quick recap and proposed next steps on the auth/keys side so your infra team can evaluate: 

TL;DR: For PoC we recommend short-lived API keys minted by a Finex service account (no manual key rotation), then for production move to JWT-backed service-account tokens with KMS-managed signing keys and automated rotation. Details below.

What we covered:
- SDK bootstrapping: embedding + tool-calling samples (we'll share a trimmed init guide).
- Routing: low-latency requests (alerts) -> dedicated model route; enrichment batch -> quantized cheaper model.
- Auth options: API keys (fast), OAuth/JWT (recommended prod), service accounts with KMS.

Proposed next actions (week of Aug 30):
1) Your infra to confirm whether Finex prefers a service-account IAM flow or relying on an internal token broker.
2) Redwood SE (Monica) to send an integration pack with sample JWT claims and rotation YAML.
3) Agree on PoC TTL: we suggest 1 hour short-lived tokens for API-key-based PoC.
4) Identify contact for compliance checklist (SOC2 evidence) — Samir to confirm.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-init-guide.pdf (SDK snippets), rotation-template.yaml (example cron + KMS key policy).

If that matches your sense, I'll loop in Monica and Ben to propose a minimal PoC timeline.

Thanks,
Connor
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

--
Attachment(s): redwood-sdk-init-guide.pdf (excerpted), rotation-template.yaml (example)
From: Ritika Sharma <ritika@finex.io>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.inference>
Cc: Samir Desai <samir@finex.io>
Date: 2027-08-22T18:13:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finex integration: post-demo handoff — auth + routing options

Connor, thanks — that lines up with what we discussed. A few clarifying Qs for your team: 

- For the PoC, we prefer the fastest path that avoids adding a new infra component. API keys with automation are OK as long as we can enforce a short TTL and rotate remotely.
- For production we will require signing keys stored in our cloud KMS and a JWT approach so we can audit tokens per-service.
- Do you support token introspection endpoints or just signature verification on the service side?

Samir will be the primary infra contact (cc) — he'll want the rotation YAML and a quick sketch of how Redwood recommends issuing short-lived keys from our side.

Can Monica/Ben propose a 30–45 minute technical handoff next Tue?

Best,
Ritika
Head of Integrations — Finex Solutions
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.inference>
To: Ritika Sharma <ritika@finex.io>
Cc: Samir Desai <samir@finex.io>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-08-23T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finex integration: post-demo handoff — auth + routing options

Ritika — perfect, thanks for the direction. Monica and Ben are looped; Monica will own the technical handoff. A few quick answers now: 

- Token introspection: Redwood supports signature verification (JWT) natively in the runtime, and we can enable an introspection endpoint on a Dedicated/Private deployment. For hosted API we recommend stateless JWT verification against the KMS public key (faster) and optional introspection via our control plane if you want token revocation semantics.

- PoC flow (minimal):
  1) Finex creates a service account in your IAM (name: finex-redwood-poc).
  2) Issue short-lived API keys from your broker with TTL=1h; Redwood SDK accepts and rotates keys automatically (see guide).
  3) We validate routing by tagging requests: X-Route: alert-low-latency or X-Route: batch-enrich.

- Production flow (recommended):
  - Use JWT signed by your KMS (RSA-pss or ES256).
  - Token claims: iss=finex-iam, sub=service-name, aud=redwood, exp ~ 5m for request tokens or 1h for inter-service (we included a sample in rotation-template.yaml).
  - Redwood runtime validates signature and enforces per-token rate-limits & route policy.

Monica/BEN: could you propose two slots next Tue (Aug 30) 10:00–11:00 or 14:00–15:00 PT? We'll include a short demo of SDK init (embedding + structured output), auth flows, and a quick reranker embedding sample.

Connor
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>
To: Ritika Sharma <ritika@finex.io>, Samir Desai <samir@finex.io>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-08-24T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finex integration: post-demo handoff — auth + routing options

Hi Ritika / Samir — thanks, looping in Marissa for pricing/committed capacity notes. Short tech handoff below and the items I'll bring to the call.

What I'll bring to the handoff (attached YAML + guide):
- rotation-template.yaml: example KeyRotation CronJob + sample KMS policy (rotate every 30 days, auto-promote new key after 24h).
- redwood-sdk-init-guide.pdf: minimal init for Node/Python including examples for:
  * embeddings endpoint + vector store hints (dimensionality, batching shard size).
  * structured output for tool-calls (how to register function schemas).
  * simple reranker pipeline: embed -> kNN candidate retrieval -> model-based rerank (we include a perf note).

Recommended PoC config (single-week):
- Auth: short-lived API key TTL=1h; Redwood SDK refreshes via a single endpoint you expose (token broker).
- Routing headers: X-Redwood-Route: realtime-alerts, batch-enrich. For host mapping we can pin route->model in the console during PoC.
- Security: require MFA on your service account and use KMS for prod signing. We attach a one-page compliance checklist (mfa-requirements.xlsx).

Sample JWT claim (example, do not reuse as-is):
- Header: {"alg":"ES256","typ":"JWT"}
- Payload: {"iss":"https://iam.finex.io","sub":"service:enricher","aud":"redwood-api","iat":1692857000,"exp":1692857400,"scope":"inference:invoke"}

Open question for your infra: do you prefer tokens minted by an internal broker (we will call introspection occasionally) or direct KMS-signed tokens? If internal broker, we recommend a refresh endpoint at /internal/v1/tokens/issue with mutual TLS.

Proposed meeting: Tue Aug 30, 10:00 PT (we'll send a calendar invite after you confirm).

—Monica
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

--
Attachment(s): rotation-template.yaml, redwood-sdk-init-guide.pdf, mfa-requirements.xlsx

Subject: Re: Finex integration: post-demo handoff — auth + routing options

Thanks Monica — Tue Aug 30 10:00 PT works. We'll target API-key PoC first (internal broker + short TTL) and then schedule a prod flow meeting to validate KMS signing and token revocation requirements.

I'll review the attachments and share an infra contact for the mutual-TLS refresh endpoint if we go that route.

Samir
Platform Engineer — Finex Solutions
